questions.q: Why is loading 500,000 records through 500,000 separate REST POST calls a poor approach?
options: It's slow, risks hitting API rate limits, and each of the half-million calls can fail independently
REST does not support the POST verb
Salesforce blocks any org from making more than 10 REST calls total
POST calls cannot create Contact records
questions.explain: Making one REST call per record at real scale is slow, burns through API request allocations quickly, and introduces many independent points of failure — exactly what Bulk API exists to avoid.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Bulk API 1.0 and Bulk API 2.0?
options: Bulk API 1.0 is REST-only and 2.0 is SOAP-only
Bulk API 1.0 is synchronous and 2.0 is not asynchronous at all
Bulk API 2.0 is a simpler, pure-REST API where Salesforce manages batching automatically, versus 1.0 where the caller manages batches manually
There is no real difference between the two versions
questions.explain: Bulk API 2.0 simplified the model by having Salesforce handle optimal batching/chunking internally, rather than requiring the caller to split data into batches itself.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the Bulk API 2.0 job lifecycle stages?
options: Retrieve results, poll for completion, upload data, close job, create job
Close job, create job, retrieve results, poll for completion, upload data
Upload data, create job, retrieve results, close job, poll for completion
Create job, upload data, close job, poll for completion, retrieve results
questions.explain: The job always starts with creation, then data upload, then closing the job to begin processing, then polling until it's done, then retrieving results.

questions.q: What operation types can a Bulk API 2.0 ingest job perform?
options: insert, update, upsert, or delete
Only insert
Only queries (SOQL)
Only metadata deployment
questions.explain: An ingest job's operation field specifies one of insert, update, upsert, or delete for the target object.

questions.q: For which of these scenarios does this lesson recommend Bulk API 2.0 over the REST API?
options: A support agent looking up a single Case record while on a call with a customer
A one-time migration of 3 million historical Order records into Salesforce
A mobile app checking a single Account's balance in real time
A webpage displaying one Contact's details as the page loads
questions.explain: Bulk API 2.0 exists for exactly this kind of large-volume, non-time-critical load — the other three scenarios are single-record, real-time lookups better suited to REST.
